NONE: › to unfasten something that is tied with laces, for example shoes
解開（鞋子）上的帶子

example: She began to unlace her boots.
她開始解開靴子上的帶子。

NONE: › not graceful or polite, or not behaving in a way that is thought to be socially acceptable for a woman
（女性）不優雅的，不禮貌的，舉止不像個淑女的

example: She was sweating in a most unladylike manner.
她出汗的樣子一點都不淑女。
Opposite
ladylike

NONE: › not allowed by law
法律禁止的；違法的
› Unleaded petrol or other substance does not contain lead.
（汽油或其他物質）無鉛的
› unleaded petrol
無鉛汽油

example: Cars these days all use unleaded petrol.
現在的汽車都使用無鉛汽油。
The price of unleaded fell again.
無鉛汽油的價格又下跌了。

NONE: › to make an effort to forget your usual way of doing something so that you can learn a new and sometimes better way
改掉，拋棄（舊習）

example: I had to unlearn the way I played guitar when I started taking formal lessons.
開始正規學習吉他的時候，我不得不丟掉以前彈吉他的習慣。

NONE: › to suddenly release a violent force that cannot be controlled
突然釋放；使爆發

example: At worst, nuclear war could be unleashed.
最壞的情況是，可能會爆發核戰爭。
Rachel's arrival on the scene had unleashed passions in him that he could scarcely control.
瑞秋的到來激起了他難以抑制的熱情。

NONE: › Unleavened bread or similar food that is made without yeast and is therefore flat.
（麵包或類似食品）未發酵的，未用酵母的，死麵的
B1 except if
除非；除了在…的情況下

example: You can't get a job unless you have experience (= you can only get a job if you have experience).
除非有工作經驗，否則你找不到工作。
Unless you call me to say you're not coming, I'll see you at the theatre (= I will see you there if you do not call to say you are not coming).
除非你打電話說你不來了，否則我就在劇院等你。

NONE: › not having a licence (= a document giving legal permission) to do something, for example to sell alcohol, or use or own something, for example a gun
無營業執照的；未經授權許可的

example: an unlicensed restaurant
無牌照經營的餐廳

NONE: B2 different from
不像；與…不同
C2 not typical or characteristic of
非…的特點，不像（…的典型樣子）
› (on a social networking website) to show that you no longer think that something is good, by clicking a button
（社群網站上，用來表示你不喜歡某事物的）「不喜歡」按鍵

example: Dan's actually very nice, unlike his father.
丹可不像他父親，他實際上人很不錯。
Unlike you, I'm not a great dancer.
我可不像你，我不太會跳舞。
It's unlike you to be quiet - is something wrong?
這麽安靜可不是你的風格——出甚麽事了嗎？
If you don't want to see his posts any more, unlike his Facebook page.
如果你不再想看他的發言，就對他的臉書頁面取消贊。

NONE: B1 not probable or likely to happen
不大可能發生的

only before noun: › [ only before noun ] not the same as you would usually expect
C2 [ only before noun ] probably not true
難以相信的，不能信服的

example: [ + (that) ] It's pretty unlikely (that) they'll turn up now - it's nearly ten o'clock.
他們現在不大可能來了——都快十點了。
He's an unlikely-looking doctor (= he is not what I expect a doctor to look like).
他看上去不太像個醫生。
When I asked what he was doing there, he came up with some unlikely explanation.
當我問他在那裡做什麼的時候，他的解釋令人難以信服。

NONE: B2 not limited; having the greatest possible amount, number, or level
不受限制的；無窮的；無數的

example: Passes are available for one month's unlimited travel within Europe.
現在可申請在歐洲無限制乘車一個月的旅行卡。
Demand for healthcare appears virtually unlimited.
看來對衛生保健的需求實際上是沒有止境的。

NONE: › not included in a list of stock exchange company prices
（證券）未掛牌的，未上市的
› US UK ex-directory not included in the public list of phone numbers belonging to the customers of a telephone company
未登入公共電話簿的

example: Doctors most often have unlisted home phone numbers to protect their privacy.
爲了保護自己的隱私，醫生們通常不把自己的住宅電話號碼登在公共電話簿上。

I or T: C1 [ I or T ] to remove the contents of something, especially a load of goods from a vehicle, the bullets from a gun or the film from a camera
除去（內容物）；（尤指）卸（貨）；從（槍）中退出子彈；從（相機）中取出膠捲
› [ I or T ] informal to tell someone about your problems, the things that worry you, etc.
I: › [ I ] US informal to express strong emotions such as anger freely to another person

example: We watched a ship unloading (sacks of flour).
我們觀看了一艘貨輪卸下（麵粉）。
I've been unloading my worries on poor Ann here.
我把自己的擔憂都一股腦兒傾倒給可憐的安了。
I was so stressed out, I just needed to unload.
我極度緊張，就是需要發洩一下。

NONE: B2 to open something, especially a door that is locked (= fastened with a lock) using a key or an electronic device
打開；（尤指用鎖匙或電子設備）開（門）
› to discover important new facts about something
解開…之謎；發現…的秘密
› to make the imagination more active, producing interesting ideas and images
開啟想像力

example: I think I left the garage door unlocked.
我覺得我忘了鎖上車庫門。
A chemical has been discovered that may be the key to unlocking the mysteries of Parkinson's disease.
已發現一種化學物質，這可能是解開帕金森氏病之謎的鎖匙。
One of poetry's functions is to unlock the imagination.
詩歌的功能之一便是開啓想像力。

NONE: › not expected
未預料到的，始料不及的
› not easy to love
不可愛的，難讓人愛上的
› not loved
無人喜愛的

example: He found himself alone and unloved.
他覺得自己孤零零一個人，沒人疼愛。

NONE: B1 not lucky
不幸的，不走運的，倒楣的

example: The couple were unlucky enough to be in the hotel when the terrorist group struck.
當恐怖集團襲擊這家旅館時，很不幸這對夫婦正住在裡面。
